companies.name: HillWebs
companies.why: Your closest local comparison—and the design reference you already liked. Study how one person explains the work and builds trust.
companies.sells: Custom websites, redesigns, Google Business Profile setup and management, local SEO, advertising support, and ongoing website care.
companies.flow: Clear local introduction → services → real website projects → process and questions → contact.
ideas: Local, personal introduction
Explain who Hayden is, the towns he serves, and how a business owner can reach him.
A page for each clear customer need
Separate the website, Google profile, and ongoing support so visitors can understand each job.
Named website examples
Show a real project, what was built, and a link visitors can try. Keep HJS demos labeled honestly.
companies.avoid: Copying the scenery, identity, or full service menu. Borrow the clarity and local relevance; offer only work you can reliably deliver.
companies.evidence: Its portfolio documents named South Sound website projects. That shows work exists; these pages do not establish its revenue, conversion rate, or a “top performer” ranking.

companies.name: Whitespark
companies.why: The clearest comparison for understanding what ongoing Google profile work can include.
companies.sells: Managed Google Business Profiles, a broader option that also improves the website, plus separate tools and directory-listing services.
companies.flow: Choose the problem → compare included work → understand account access and reporting → ask for help.
ideas: Separate setup from ongoing care
Fixing a profile once and looking after it every month are different jobs. Explain what continues after setup.
A tangible monthly checklist
Show examples of real work: correcting hours, adding owner-supplied photos, reviewing changes, and reporting activity.
Clear ownership and access
Explain that the owner keeps control of the profile and adds the service provider as a manager.
companies.avoid: Treating weekly posts as a guaranteed ranking improvement, or calling profile button taps completed phone calls.
companies.evidence: Whitespark publishes a four-profile, year-over-year case study reporting increases in phone interactions and website clicks. It is company-published and anonymized, not independently audited.

companies.name: Sterling Sky
companies.why: Useful for learning what broader local SEO involves and how to explain evidence responsibly.
companies.sells: Ongoing local search work across the Google profile, website content, technical issues, and relevant links—not simply changing profile fields.
companies.flow: Investigate → prioritize useful changes → do the work → report and review.
ideas: Diagnose before choosing a package
Start with the business’s actual problem. An inaccurate listing, weak website, and untracked ad campaign need different fixes.
Explain the next useful action
A monthly update should say what changed, what was observed, and what you will work on next.
Problem → work → evidence
When HJS has results, explain the starting point, work performed, period measured, and metric.
companies.avoid: Selling its broad agency scope before you have the skills and capacity, or attributing a mixed marketing campaign’s results to profile care alone.
companies.evidence: Its named LawnSavers case study reports more organic conversions and leads after a mix of website, profile, links, tracking, and advertising work. Agency-reported evidence; individual effects are not isolated.

companies.name: Hook Agency
companies.focus: Websites connected to ongoing contractor marketing
companies.why: A useful model for showing how a website leads into continuing work for a specific type of business.
companies.sells: Contractor websites, local SEO, Google profile work, paid search, Local Services Ads, and Meta campaigns.
companies.flow: Who it helps → business problems → how the relationship works → services and examples → next conversation.
ideas: Speak to a recognizable customer
Use examples from local trades, shops, and other businesses you actually work with.
Explain what happens after launch
Connect the website to future updates, search improvements, or ads when that business has a reason for them.
Show the ongoing routine
Make monthly work visible: changes completed, inquiries tracked, and the next action agreed with the owner.
companies.avoid: Copying its larger-agency scope or commitments. A website cost spread over twelve payments is not the same as ongoing maintenance revenue.
companies.evidence: Hook publishes a named Genz-Ryan website/SEO case study with qualified organic lead figures. These are agency-reported; the total lead figure’s measurement window is not clearly identified.

companies.name: WebFX
companies.why: Useful for understanding how many services fit together. Borrow its organization selectively.
companies.sells: Websites, content, maintenance, local SEO, business listings, paid advertising, and connected reporting.
companies.flow: Business objective → relevant services → evidence and process → proposal or contact.
ideas: Group work by the customer’s goal
Help people find the business, understand the offer, contact the owner, or come back again.
Describe deliverables before terminology
“Keep your hours and services current” is easier to understand than an unexplained SEO label.
Separate activity from business results
Explain the difference between a profile click, an inquiry, a booked job, and revenue.
companies.avoid: A huge menu, a complicated dashboard, or language implying HJS has a large specialist team. Keep the direct relationship with Hayden.
companies.evidence: Its Merrimack Valley Psychological Associates case study reports revenue growth during combined website/content and local-search work. Provider/client testimony, not independently audited attribution.
